ocr.title: Get text from a photo or PDF
ocr.help: Choose a PDF, or photos of book pages. The text is read on this device — free, and nothing is sent anywhere. You then check it and add it to the content.
ocr.languageHint: Pick only what is on the page — it reads faster and makes fewer mistakes.
ocr.tipPdf: A typed PDF gives exact text, maths symbols included. Old Hindi PDFs in the Kruti Dev font are turned into proper Hindi.
ocr.tipPhoto: Take a photo uses this device's camera (the webcam on a computer). Hold the page flat, in good light, and fill the frame. Printed text works best; handwriting is often wrong.
ocr.tipMaths: Maths in photos is often misread (x² becomes x2). Fix it with the Σ maths symbols button in the editor.
ocr.tipFirstTime: The first time, this device downloads the reading tools (about 8 MB). After that it starts at once.
ocr.wrongType: Choose a PDF, or photos (JPG, PNG or WebP).
ocr.failed: The file could not be read. Try a clearer photo, or another PDF.
ocr.firstPages: Only the first {{count}} of {{total}} pages were read. Add the rest in another go.
ocr.readingHint: You can check the pages already read below while the rest are read.
ocr.check: Check the text against each page before adding it — words in photos, Hindi vowel signs and maths are sometimes read wrong.

how.REPAIRED: read from the page — the PDF’s own text was damaged

ocr.kruti: Old Hindi font (Kruti Dev) — convert to Hindi
ocr.useCopied: Use the PDF’s own text instead (exact English and maths, damaged Hindi)
